issues.description: Silent None return from extract_arch_from_url produces a malformed URL containing the literal 'None'.
issues.detail: When the regex misses, the function returns None and the caller formats it into '.../latest/None/Packages/...', shipping a broken URL with no error. Either raise on miss or have the caller refuse to continue. This is defensive-as-substitute-for-correctness, and it lets a missing fact flow downstream as a string-shaped fact.

issues.description: nevra[0] uses the first character of the filename, not the first letter of the package name as koji's layout requires.
issues.detail: Koji's Packages directory is keyed by the first letter of the package NAME, lowercased. Taking nevra[0] from the URL basename happens to work for typical NEVRAs but is silently wrong for any deviation (leading paths, casing, unstated precondition). Parse the package name properly rather than relying on an unstated invariant.

issues.description: Arch detection scans the whole URL by regex instead of reading the arch from the NEVRA filename suffix.
issues.detail: Every RPM filename ends in .<arch>.rpm, the canonical source. Regex-searching the entire URL path means a segment like '/ppc64le-mirror/.../foo.x86_64.rpm' silently mis-classifies. Two sources of truth (filename suffix vs URL scan) can disagree. Read arch from the NEVRA suffix, or thread it in from the caller which already knows.

issues.description: Acknowledged race with coreos-koji-tagger is shipped with no mitigation, invariant, or in-code note.
issues.detail: The commit message concedes the URL is fabricated before the artifact is tagged into coreos-pool, then asserts safety without stating an invariant, retry, or detection. The temporal assumption lives only in the PR body, not the code. Add a code comment naming the assumption and a retry/verify step so a future 404 debug takes minutes, not hours.

issues.description: Hard-coded koji_url_base and arch list are duplicated constants without a single source of truth.
issues.detail: The arch list inside extract_arch_from_url is independent of the arches generate_main iterates over, and the koji base URL is a string literal buried in logic. A change to either silently invalidates the other. Lift both to module-level constants (or a small layout descriptor) so the koji repo shape is named data, not inlined string concatenation.

issues.description: Stale 'Prioritize the url from fedora-coreos-pool' branch left in query_packages_location with no rationale after the new pass rewrites everything.
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only now rewrites URLs downstream, so the older prioritization is either dead weight or load-bearing for a reason that should be stated. Leaving both halves of a half-finished refactor in the tree is a smuggled assumption. Remove it or add a comment explaining why it still matters.

synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The panel agrees the approach — synthesize the koji URL because dnf5 returns wrong baseurls — is reasonable, but the execution has two correctness defects: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None and lets the literal 'None' be formatted into the URL, and nevra[0] conflates filename-first-character with package-name-first-letter (works today by accident). The arch should be read from the NEVRA suffix, not regex-scanned from the whole URL, which is two sources of truth that can disagree. The acknowledged race with coreos-koji-tagger is shipped without mitigation or in-code comment, and hard-coded constants are scattered across functions instead of named once at module level.
